decision: the issuer and resource are publicUrl itself; every path derives from it: the endpoint, <path>/oauth/{authorize,token,register,redmine/callback}, RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 path-inserted well-known URLs, both OpenID Connect discovery URLs, and a copy of the protected resource metadata at <path>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, which the 401 names

decision: everything handed out is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key HKDF-derived from the secret per purpose (registration, browser, consent, state, code, access, refresh), with the issuer as associated data; previousSecret opens but never seals
why: no database on Node or Workers; a value of one purpose or one deployment never opens as another; rotation without signing everyone out

decision: codes from Redmine sign-in are single-use because Redmine's code is spent only at our token endpoint; a per-process cache also refuses a redeemed code id; API-key codes live 60 s, PKCE- and resource-bound, and can be replayed once per other process within that minute
why: OAuth 2.1 single use without a store; the fallback has no upstream single-use, so its residual risk is documented
evidence: unit: second exchange of a code refused for both sign-in methods; README trade-offs

decision: a sealed __Host-redmine-mcp-oauth cookie (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/) carries a browser nonce; the sealed consent form value and the sealed Redmine state both carry it, and the consent POST is refused when Origin names another origin
why: CSRF on the consent form, and the confused deputy where Redmine auto-approves a returning user: a Redmine link started by someone else comes back to a browser without the nonce and gets an error page, never a code; the __Host- name cannot collide with _redmine_session and is never forwarded
evidence: unit: consent POST without cookie, with another browser's cookie, with a forged value, from another Origin; callback in another browser is 403 without redirect

decision: pages escape every value, send a nonce-based style-src CSP, frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy same-origin, and a form-action that lists Redmine's public origin and the client's redirect origin
why: client names are attacker-chosen; Chrome enforces form-action on the redirect after a form post, so 'self' alone would block the decision; same-origin keeps the Origin header on the consent POST
evidence: unit: <script> client name rendered escaped; CSP and headers asserted

decision: metadata documents: https, normalized URL, a path, no port or credentials, no IP literal or local name, no redirects followed, 5 s, 5 KB, cached 5 minutes; a document with client_secret or a non-https non-loopback redirect URI is refused; unknown fields such as claude.ai's jwt-bearer grant are ignored; the Node CLI fetches through publicFetch, which checks every resolved address inside the connection's own lookup; Workers need global_fetch_strictly_public
why: SSRF through attacker-chosen client_id URLs, including DNS rebinding between check and connect
evidence: unit: ten refused client_id shapes, redirect and oversize refused; publicFetch refuses private literals and localhost and lets 1.1.1.1 through; live fetch of the claude.ai and vscode.dev documents through the built server

decision: Dynamic Client Registration returns the sealed registration as client_id, forces token_endpoint_auth_method none, and accepts only https or loopback http redirect URIs, refusing custom schemes; loopback redirect URIs match on any port; the client host allowlist checks a document's host or every redirect host of a registration
why: Cursor needs DCR; Claude Code and Codex pick random loopback ports (RFC 8252); the MCP spec allows only https and localhost redirects; a registration names no verifiable host but its redirects
evidence: unit: official MCP client registers and signs in with a different loopback port; custom scheme, javascript:, fragment and plain http refused

decision: scopes redmine:read, redmine:write, redmine:delete are hierarchical and map to read-only, no-delete and full; the server's mode caps them and is what its 401 and metadata ask for; no requested scope means all offered; a refresh may narrow; each scope asks Redmine for its permission list (20 read, 50 write with use_webhooks for a declared 7.0 only, 10 delete_*), never admin
why: Redmine grants only requested permissions and refuses unknown ones (6.1 lacks use_webhooks); issue edits ignore token scope (#44271), so the access mode stays the guard; OAuth sessions acting as admin would surprise
evidence: permission lists dumped from Redmine 6.1 (79) and 7.0 (80) with rails runner; unit: read token lists 43 tools, delete request on a no-delete server gets read and write

decision: our access token lives min(1 h, Redmine's expires_in - 60 s), our refresh token 30 days per refresh; a refresh with the other sign-in method's grant fails
why: never outlive the Redmine token inside; turning apiKeyLogin off must end key-based grants
evidence: unit: expired after an hour; key grant refused after switching to redmineApp; contract: refresh against real Doorkeeper, old refresh token refused once the new access token was used

decision: a request without credentials gets 401 with Bearer resource_metadata and scope and no error code (RFC 6750 3.1); invalid, expired or foreign-audience tokens get the SDK's invalid_token challenge; a token with none of our scopes gets 403 insufficient_scope; X-Redmine-API-Key wins over Authorization
why: spec and SDK behaviour; header mode unchanged
evidence: unit: verifier seam tests through the handler

decision: grant store as the owner decided: GrantStore is two operations on namespaced keys, an atomic consume(key, ttl) and has(key); family revocation is consume and has on family:<id>; with a store, codes of both sign-in methods, Redmine states and consent pages are single-use across instances, refresh tokens carry an id and a family and work once, a reused code or refresh token ends the family, and access tokens of an ended family are refused; memoryGrantStore() ships in the main entry and the CLI uses it by default
why: Fable M2 and I2, Codex H2, M3 and M7: stateless sealing cannot make anything single-use or revocable; two operations are the least a Durable Object, Redis or a database adapter must implement
evidence: unit: rotation and family end, code reuse ends its tokens, API-key code refused by a second handler sharing the store, state replayed in the same browser refused; workerd: the README's Durable Object adapter, verbatim, passes flow, state replay, rotation, family end and code reuse for both sign-in methods

decision: without a store: codes, states and consent pages stay single-use per process through a memory store, refresh tokens do not rotate, families are not checked, and an API-key grant carries an absolute end 30 days after consent that refreshes cannot extend
why: owner decision; a per-process family check would disagree between instances, so it is not attempted
evidence: unit: API-key refresh refused at day 31 without a store and accepted with one; a second handler without the store accepts a code once (documented)

decision: a code or refresh token is checked with has() before the call to Redmine and marked with consume() after it, and a failed consume ends the family
why: Fable L4: marking first burnt the code on a Redmine outage; Redmine's own single use and the post-call consume still close the race
evidence: unit: 502 then 200 for both the code exchange and the refresh, with and without a store

decision: publicFetch gives 204, 205 and 304 no body, and any throw in the response callback destroys the response and rejects; fec0::/10, 64:ff9b:1::/48 and 192.88.99.0/24 are blocked
why: Codex H1 (process crash on 205), Fable L2 and Codex M5
evidence: unit with a mocked https and dns transport that answers asynchronously and runs the real publicLookup: 8 tests fail on the old code, one with the uncaught error

decision: oauth.fetchClientMetadata is required at the type and at creation; a non-200 metadata answer says only could not be fetched; the README gives the real reason for global_fetch_strictly_public (same-zone fetches go through the front door)
why: Fable M3 and Codex M4: the global fetch was an unguarded default for embedders, and the status was an oracle
evidence: unit: creation refused without it; 404, 401, 500 and 302 give the same message

decision: a metadata document or registration declaring a token_endpoint_auth_method other than none is refused; registrations take at most 5 redirect URIs of 256 characters and a 100-character name
why: Codex M6: silently downgrading a confidential client; Fable I4: unbounded client_id size
evidence: unit: private_key_jwt document refused, none accepted; client_secret_basic and private_key_jwt registrations refused; largest registration under 2600 characters

decision: scope: absent or empty means everything offered, names that are not ours next to ours are ignored, none of ours is refused before consent; a refresh naming a scope the grant lacks gets invalid_scope

evidence: unit: openid offline_access and redmine:raed refused; redmine:read openid grants read; refresh with redmine:delete or profile refused

decision: our access token lives min(1 h, expires_in - min(60, floor(expires_in / 2))) and expires_in must be a positive integer; redirect_uri at the token endpoint is compared only when sent
why: Fable L3 and Codex L10 (tokens expired on issue), Fable L1 (OAuth 2.1 clients omit redirect_uri)
evidence: unit: Redmine 30 s gives 15 s and works, 1 s gives 1 s; exchange without redirect_uri succeeds

decision: Authorization must match ^Bearer +b64token$ case-insensitively; publicUrl must equal its canonical identifier (lowercase host, no default port, no trailing slash, no dot segments); the secret needs 32 characters and 12 distinct ones, and the messages say a passphrase is not random

evidence: unit: trailing fields and two credentials refused, lowercase scheme and two spaces accepted; five non-canonical spellings refused with the canonical one named; repeated patterns refused, random hex accepted

evidence: unit: four wrong keys re-render, the fifth ends it, the first page is refused as already sent, Redmine saw five checks

decision: N1: a spent code or refresh token leaves a 30-second recent:<id> marker; a second use while it lives is refused with invalid_grant and the sign-in stays; later reuse ends the family; the marker is written just before the id is consumed, after Redmine answered, so the losing request of a race always finds it, and the pre-check sets nothing, so a late reuse is still caught
why: Fable round 2 N1: strict rotation signed people out when their own client refreshed twice at once or retried an exchange; marking after the consume would leave a gap a concurrent loser could fall into on a store whose calls interleave
evidence: unit: concurrent refresh pairs and concurrent code exchanges in both sign-in methods, with a Doorkeeper-like upstream, keep the winner's tokens (all four fail on the old code); in-window reuse at 5 s refused without an end, reuse at 31 s ends the family; workerd: the same race and a real 31 s late replay through the Durable Object store

decision: N2: a registration asking for client_secret_basic or client_secret_post, or naming no method, is answered token_endpoint_auth_method none; private_key_jwt, tls_client_auth, self_signed_tls_client_auth and unknown methods stay refused; metadata documents still need none or no method
why: Fable round 2 N2: RFC 7591 lets the registrar replace the method, and an omitted method means client_secret_basic, so refusing the explicit spellings was inconsistent

decision: N3: an empty or over-long client_name is dropped from a registration instead of refusing it

evidence: unit: empty, blank and 101-character names register without a name

decision: N4: the consent form runs at most 4 key checks at Redmine at once per process and answers others with a 503 page to retry from; with a store, a browser nonce may fail 10 keys an hour (keyfail:<nonce>:<slot> keys, 1 hour), then gets 429; the README says none of this limits a source address and suggests a proxy limit on POST to the consent page
why: Fable round 2 N4: a fresh sign-in restarted the five-key count, so the page stayed a cheap oracle; a per-address limit needs the address, which the handler does not trust
evidence: unit: a fifth check while four are held at Redmine gets 503 and retries from its page; two five-key chains in one browser, then 429, Redmine saw ten checks, another browser unaffected; both fail on the old code

decision: I-7: when Redmine did not answer, the re-rendered page and the page that ends the sign-in say so, with 503; it still counts toward the five

evidence: unit: five unanswered checks, the last page says Redmine did not answer and not too many keys

decision: I-1: a configured store is wrapped so a throw or rejection becomes StoreUnavailable; the token endpoint answers 503 temporarily_unavailable, the consent form and Redmine's return a 503 error page, the MCP endpoint 503 when a verifier cannot tell; onError gets the cause
